idea: Themed weeks, week four, Money day: written from the source, then corrected by a numbers editor and a viewer editor before voicing.
description: At public-sector banks, the gold loans outstanding on 31 March 2026 that were reported for Tamil Nadu were 36.4% of the all-state total, while Tamil Nadu had 5.4% of India's projected population. Against Kerala, Tamil Nadu had 4.9 times the gold loans and 2.1 times the people. Andhra Pradesh's share was 19.7%.

Per person that is ₹53,085 of public-bank gold loans reported for Tamil Nadu; India, about ₹7,900. Public-sector banks only: the RBI keeps no state figures, and private banks and finance companies are excluded. The answer prints no total, so shares are of its state rows. The amount is the loan book (rupees outstanding), not bad loans and not weight of gold. People are projected population, National Commission on Population (July 2020 edition). The table shows how much, not why.
source: Ministry of Finance, Lok Sabha unstarred question 3648, 10 Aug 2026, Annexure I: gold loans outstanding (the loan book, not bad loans) at public sector banks, by state, 31 March 2026, as reported by the banks. The RBI keeps no state figure; private banks and finance companies are excluded. The answer prints no total: shares are of the state rows (two small UT rows, ₹192 crore, are left out). People: projected population, 1 March 2026, National Commission on Population (July 2020 edition). Rupees, not weight of gold.
